title: Implement chemisorption model
action: Implement the semiempirical chemisorption model Hamiltonian for hydrogen on nickel. Use the Slater orbital parameters for H (1s exponent from Slater's rules, 2p orbitals with specified parameters), the nickel s- and d-band wavefunctions from the Appendix, the effective density of states approximated by seven δ functions for the s band and one δ function for the d band, and the parameter B = 0.222 (as given for Ni). Construct the overlap matrix elements, the metal local orbitals via Eq. (6), and the model coupling terms. Include the 1s–s and 2p–d interactions, with the 2s orbital neglected after orthogonalization.

title: Compute potential energy surfaces
action: For each of the three Ni surface orientations—(111), (100), and (110)—set up a grid of lateral adsorption positions across the surface unit cell. At each position, determine the equilibrium vertical distance by maximizing the overlap between the hydrogen 2p orbitals and the metal d wavefunctions, then compute the total electronic energy of the H+Ni system. Calculate the adsorption energy as the difference between the H+surface energy and the sum of the clean surface energy plus the isolated H atom’s energy. Store the adsorption energy at every grid point.

title: Write adsorption energies at most favorable sites
action: From the energy scans, identify the adsorption energy value at the energetically most favorable site on each surface. Write a CSV file with the surface label and the corresponding adsorption energy (in kcal/mol).
description: Adsorption energies (kcal/mol) for hydrogen on Ni(111), Ni(100), and Ni(110) at the most favorable adsorption site, as computed by the semiempirical model.
output_schema: surface (string), adsorption_energy_kcal_per_mol (float). Rows: Ni(111), Ni(100), Ni(110).

title: Write energy variation on Ni(111)
action: From the Ni(111) energy scan, compute the maximum variation of the adsorption energy across the surface unit cell (maximum energy minus minimum energy). Write a CSV file containing this single value in kcal/mol.
description: Maximum variation of the adsorption energy across the Ni(111) surface unit cell (kcal/mol).
